title: auth: revokeAllUserSessions returns 0 with no throw when the session store is down, so the admin status change and the user-erasure subscriber silently revoke nothing (session.ts:317-318)
description:
## BLUF

`revokeAllUserSessions` **answers** `0` **and does NOT throw when the Redis session store is unreachable** (`services/auth/src/services/session.ts:317-318`: `if (!redisAvailable) return 0;`). Two callers treat that `0` as "there was nothing to revoke" and carry on reporting success. The sessions then validate again when Redis recovers.

**The same module throws in the same condition elsewhere:** `createSession` at `:156` raises `'Redis is not available — cannot create session'`. The inconsistency is the defect.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling after gate BO1 on PR #1655, which measured this failure mode on the password-reset route. **The two password routes are fixed in that PR** by a route-local guard; these two callers are deliberately out of KS-1407's scope and are why this ticket exists.

## Recommendation

Either make the shared function fail closed (a strict variant, or a throw plus an explicit opt-out for callers that genuinely tolerate a no-op), or give each caller its own availability check. It is a **wider ruling than one ticket's scope** because it changes behaviour for every caller at once, which is exactly why PR #1655 did not take it.

## The enumeration (every product caller, measured)

| caller | file:line | what it does with the `0` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **user-erasure subscriber** | `services/auth/src/services/userErasedSubscriber.ts:50` | `const sessionsRevoked = await revokeAllUserSessions(userId);` — an **erased** subject's sessions stay live while the store is down. This is the data-protection path and the reason this is High. |
| **admin status change** | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:838` | inside `if (accountStatusForbidsCredential(updatedUser))` — the KS 796 path whose whole point is "cut the sessions this status cannot hold". With the flag false it cuts none and the status change still answers success. |
| password change / reset | `routes/users.ts`, `routes/auth.ts` | **FIXED in #1655** — both confirm the revocation is possible before the write and re-assert after it. |

Control for the enumeration: the same search shape finds `revokeSession` in **17 files**, so it is not blind.

## Why High rather than Medium

The erasure path is a data-protection obligation: an erasure that reports success while the subject's sessions remain usable is a compliance failure, not only a bug. The admin path is the KS 796 thesis — "this status cannot hold a credential" and "cut the sessions it already has" must not be able to disagree — and under this condition they disagree silently.

## Exposure, stated precisely

While the flag is false the old sessions are refused anyway, because `getSession` returns null. **The exposure is the resurrection after recovery, not the outage itself.** That is the gate's own framing of the equivalent reset case and it applies unchanged here.

## Not measured

I did not drive these two callers against a downed store myself; the mechanism is a source reading of `session.ts:317-318` plus the gate's measurement of the identical path on reset (probe B1: 200, token burned, 0 revoked, and the old session ACTIVE again after recovery). The inference is that the same `return 0` reaches these two callers; the probe for each is not run.

**Board search before filing:** `revokeAllUserSessions`, `userErasedSubscriber`, "admin status change revoke sessions redis unavailable", "revokeAllUserSessions returns 0 silently", "erased subject sessions survive". No open ticket covers this. **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated never-published token returned **0** hits and `revokeAllUserSessions` returned a hit, so the search discriminates.

Related KS-1407.

nodes.title: Refs KS-1692: a revoke that THROWS maps onto the same post-write 503

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** QA gate 245 found a third caller of the silent zero this ticket describes: the role-change revoke that PR 2075 (KS-2083) adds. If the session store's availability flag drops after a request was authenticated, the role-change PATCH answers 200 with nothing revoked. Kam's card `secuura-ks2083-session-end-race-in-flight-1107` = a, "Merge with the wording corrected, and ticket the race High (recommended)", ruled 2026-11-08 at 20:32:11 +11:00, says a seat fixes "the store-down case next on a new ticket"; this ticket already carries that case, so no second ticket was filed. Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME, the real `initRedisSession` over a fake client with the error event fired during the write. No state, assignee or priority of this ticket was changed.

**What gate 245 measured (PR 2075, head d2245bf37fe0):** 200, the role written, and a log line `sessionsRevoked: 0` at info. After the store heals, the session is live on both checks and the old token raises a second account (200). PR 2075 names a revoke that throws (500), and not this one. The class is the one KS-1407 B1 fixed on the password path; the role-change path has it too. Narrow window, silent result.

**Where (gate 245's tree):** `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/session.ts` line 332 returns 0, and `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/routes/users.ts` line 846 takes it. This ticket's description cites lines 317 and 318 of the session file on an earlier tree, and lists the status-change caller and the erasure subscriber; the role-change revoke is a third caller.

**Not measured:** real Redis, and any box.

**Source:** gate 245 verdict, finding F2 on PR 2075, `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-11-07_gate245-tier1-y-auth/verdict.md`. This seat re-read the verdict and ran nothing else.

**Gate BS1's note N1 is closed. PR #1669 is up at head `4728c1d613038a8082625f79e564837953bd7453` — a revocation that THROWS after the password write now maps onto the same post-write 503 the check-then-act path already produces, on both password doors. This is PR 1 of two: the `session.ts` half (the unguarded `del`, and the silent zero as it reaches the admin status change and the erasure subscriber) is PR 2 and is ruled separately.**

**The gap, in the gate's words:** *"A revocation that THROWS after the write is fail-closed on reset and only half fail-closed on change-password. No author cell pins either."* KS-1407 installed a flag check either side of the write, but `revokeAllUserSessions` can **reject** as well as answer a silent 0, and a throw skipped the post-write re-assert entirely and landed in `next(error)` as a **500 INTERNAL_ERROR**. BS1's probe C3 measured the change-password case: the password *was* written, the attacker session was **still ACTIVE** after recovery, and the natural retry with the old current password answered **400 "Current password is incorrect"**.

**The fix** wraps only the revoke and re-throws as the existing post-write 503, so a store that is DOWN and a store that THROWS are indistinguishable to the caller. Not `.catch(() => 0)` — that is the author's own A5 arm, which the gate measured reding **0 of 23** cells and which would convert this into a 200 with nothing revoked.

**The number that earned the cells: A5 now reds three of them.** The red-proof judges **14 cells — my 5 plus the 9 pre-existing** — so collateral is a failure, and none appeared:

| arm | failing cells |
|---|---|
| no mutation (positive control) | none, **14/14** |
| `.catch(() => 0)` on both routes | **T1 T2 T3** |
| the catch removed (throw → 500) | T1 T2 T3 |
| a swallow that continues to 200 | T1 T2 T3 |
| the "sign in again" clause restored in both 503s | **T3 alone** |
| the post-write re-assert removed | **B1-R2, B1-R3** — not my cells, proving they do not piggyback on the KS-1407 flag guard |

**Two things deliberately not done, both recorded in the PR body.** N4's line-cite half is a **no-op**: at this develop the head has exactly `session.ts:317-318` and `:156`, so the comment is accurate and editing it would make it wrong — the earlier correction was measured against a different tree. And an arm I had planned (A9: "make the revoke resolve 0, T1/T2 must not red") was **false** — a resolving revoke with a healthy store answers 200 while T1 expects 503 — so I replaced it with the independence arm above rather than run an assertion that could not hold.

**A finding now recorded in the route itself:** `authenticate()` already refuses a change-password request when the store is down, verified at source (`validateSession` → `getSession` returns null when the client is unavailable). So that route's pre-check is **defence in depth only**; the post-write mapping is the reachable half, because the store can drop between authentication and the revoke. Both halves are labelled in the code.

**Suite:** `105 files / 1132 → 1137 tests`, **+5, 0 vanished**, reaching `1137 passed, 0 failed, rc 0`. Leg 16 reports auth at `42 errors: 42 in the baseline, 0 new`, so the added test lines introduce no type errors — the gate's figure, not mine.

⚠ **Known residue:** one run of three showed `ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity` failing at **5004 ms**, the 5000 ms boundary class already in `BACKLOG.md` across six source-scanning files; my cells failed 0 times in every run. The cells inject the throw at the mock, so they pin the route's *handling* of a rejection and say nothing about which real ioredis conditions produce one. And the change-password route's two 503s now carry byte-identical messages on purpose — T3 pins the clause on both, but nothing pins that they stay equal.

## Gate BS1 adds TWO more members to this family, and one wording fix

While gating PR #1655 (KS-1407, merged `86df4f5a52cc`), gate BS1 measured two further cases of the same root cause this ticket names — `revokeAllUserSessions` not failing closed when the session store is impaired. Verdict `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-20_gate-BS1-pr1655-ks1407-r2/verdict.md` (`sed '1d;$d' | shasum -a 256` = `8480cd2c56ef` = its trailer). Both are **outside** KS-1407's diff and belong here.

### Member: a revocation that THROWS (gate note N1, MEDIUM)
The silent zero is now fail-closed on both password routes. A **throw** is not:
- **Reset (probe R3):** `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, 1 write, **0 burns**; the old session is ACTIVE after recovery, but the retry answers 200, burns once and kills it. Fail-closed.
- **Change-password (probe C3):** `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, the password **was** written, the old session is **ACTIVE** after recovery, and **the caller is told neither**. The natural retry with the old password gets `400 Current password is incorrect`.
- A `.catch(() => 0)` on either route reds **0 of the 23** KS-1407 cells, so no author cell pins this; the gate's R3 and C3 do.
- **Gate's recommended shape:** wrap the revoke in each route and map a throw onto the same post-write **503**, with the "WAS changed / WAS reset" wording, plus one cell per route.

### Member: the unguarded index delete (gate note N2, LOW-MEDIUM, `session.ts:323`)
`revokeAllUserSessions` checks the flag once at `:316`; each `revokeSession` re-checks at `:298` and returns false silently; **`redis.del(user_sessions:<id>)` at `:323` is not guarded.** Probe R4, with 3 sessions and the store flipping mid-loop: the first reset answered 503 with the token unburned, the index set was **deleted anyway**, and the retry then found an empty set, revoked 0 and answered **200 with session 3 still ACTIVE**. The gate's own realism caveat: with real ioredis the window is narrow (a command issued during an outage either resolves after `ready` or rejects, which is the N1 class). Same root as KS-1691's missing tombstone.

### Wording fix to carry in the same round (gate note N4, trivial, mine)
Two defects of my own in the merged KS-1407 code, which the gate directed here rather than to a new PR:
- change-password's post-write 503 says *"Sign in again with the new password"*, but the caller's **own** session survives that path — the gate's C2 made the advised retry on the same bearer and got 200.
- my comments cite `session.ts:317-318` and `:156`; at the merged head the silent zero is at **`:316`** and `createSession`'s throw at **`:155`**.

**This is a later tier-1 round, not now** — per Wednesday's post-merge instruction.
